name: Health Care Administrator
description: Running the non-clinical half of health care — budgets, staffing, quality, compliance, revenue, regulators. $123,860 median, 616,200 employed, 62,100 openings a year, growing much faster than average. ⚠⚠ There is no required major: Census microdata puts HEALTH first at 169,319 people, BUSINESS second at 75,396 and PSYCHOLOGY third at 47,154. ⚠⚠⚠ But Florida statute puts a price on the choice — on the nursing home side, a health administration major halves the required training programme from 2,000 hours to 1,000.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ ONE SETTING IS LICENSED AND THE REST ARE NOT. Running a hospital, a group practice, a clinic, a health plan or a surgery centre in Florida requires no state licence of any kind. ⚠ Running a NURSING HOME does: chapter 468, part II defines a nursing home administrator as a person who is licensed to engage in the practice of nursing home administration in this state, and s. 468.1695 sets out how. ⚠⚠⚠ AND THE STATUTE PRICES THE MAJOR, WHICH IS RARE AND WORTH READING TWICE. Pathway A — a baccalaureate whose major is health care administration, health services administration or an equivalent major — requires a college-affiliated internship or a 1,000-HOUR training programme. Pathway B — any other bachelor's — requires a 2,000-HOUR training programme, or one year of qualifying management experience plus 1,000 hours. ⚠⚠ So on this one route the major is worth roughly a thousand hours, which is about six months of full-time work, and it is written into law rather than into a preference. ⚠ On the rest of the occupation nothing is licensed, and what employers substitute is a master's — specifically one accredited by CAHME, the Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education. Florida's CAHME-accredited programmes sit at UCF, FIU, UNF, UF and USF. ⚠ Verify the current list with CAHME itself; it is the authority and it changes.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠ No required major — here is what people actually hold

Census ACS microdata (2024) on the undergraduate fields held by medical and health services managers:

FieldPeople
Health169,319
Business75,396
⚠ Psychology47,154

⚠ Health leads, but the two non-health fields behind it are not a rounding error — together they are close to three-quarters of the health total. And psychology in third place is not something any adviser sheet predicts, which is worth saying plainly: it is where a lot of people who ended up managing human services started.

Attainment, same source:

LevelPeople
Bachelor's degree263,934
⚠⚠ Graduate degree⚠⚠ 250,881
⚠ Some college, no degree112,767

⚠⚠⚠ Nearly as many people in this occupation hold a graduate degree as hold a bachelor's. That is a much higher graduate share than most careers on this site, and it is the single most useful planning fact here: on the management track a master's is closer to normal than to exceptional.

⚠ And 112,767 got in with some college and no degree — almost always by being promoted out of a clinical or operational job. Both doors are real. They just lead to different ceilings.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida statute answers the “does the major matter?” question in HOURS

This is a choice path, so the question is always whether the named major is worth choosing. On the long-term care side Florida answers it in law. Section 468.1695:

Your bachelor'sWhat the licence then requires
✅ health care administration, health services administration or an equivalent majora college-affiliated internship, or a 1,000-hour training programme
⚠ anything else2,000-hour training programme — or one year of qualifying management experience plus 1,000 hours

⚠⚠ The named major is worth about a thousand hours, or roughly six months of full-time work. Nothing else on this page is that concrete, and it applies to exactly one corner of the occupation — so weigh it against where you actually want to work.

⚠⚠ The access story, and it runs the opposite way from most degrees

Measured over the Florida course file, upper-division HSA coursework is carried by:

SectorInstitutions
✅ Florida College System⚠⚠ 20
State University System9

⚠⚠⚠ Twenty state colleges carry the bachelor's-level coursework against nine universities. For most baccalaureate subjects that ratio is the other way round. It means this degree can usually be finished near home, at state-college tuition, without transferring — and for a working adult already inside a hospital or a practice, that is often the whole difference between doing it and not.

⚠ The ladder narrows sharply above that. Florida's CAHME-accredited master's programmes are at UCF, FIU, UNF, UF and USF — five, all universities. Wide at the bottom, narrow at the top.

The occupation

Medical and health services managers (11-9111)
2025 median$123,860
Employed (2024)616,200
Annual openings62,100
Growth 2024–34✅ much faster than average (7% or higher)
Education46% bachelor's, 21% master's, 11% associate

⚠ Read the median with care. It spans a two-partner dental practice's office manager and a hospital system's chief operating officer. Setting and scale drive the number far more than the credential does — so when you research pay, research it by setting.

⚠⚠ The route nobody advertises: come from the clinical side

The 169,319 health-field degrees in the table above are largely clinicians who moved across — nurses above all, but also respiratory therapists, radiographers, laboratory scientists and paramedics.

⚠ It is a strong position and an underrated one. You arrive already knowing what the operation does, which is the part a classroom cannot supply, and you are credible with the staff you are managing in a way an outside hire is not.

⚠⚠ If that is you, the efficient move is the degree part-time at a state college while you keep working — which is exactly what the twenty-institution footprint above exists for.

What the work is

O*NET: direct, supervise and evaluate work activities of medical, nursing, technical, clerical, service, maintenance, and other personnel; plan, implement, and administer programs and services in a health care or medical facility; conduct and administer fiscal operations, including accounting, planning budgets, authorizing expenditures, establishing rates for services, and coordinating financial reporting; maintain awareness of advances in medicine, computerized diagnostic and treatment equipment, data processing technology, government regulations, health insurance changes, and financing options.

⚠ Notice how much of it is money and rules. Two of the four core tasks are fiscal operations and regulatory awareness — which is why the finance and law courses below are the ones to take seriously, not the survey ones.

Necessary skills

  • Reading a budget and a payer contract, and knowing which line is the one that matters.
  • Regulatory literacy — CMS conditions of participation, Joint Commission, AHCA licensure, HIPAA. Compliance failures are what end careers here.
  • Managing licensed professionals who do not report to you in practice, particularly physicians. This is the hardest part and nothing prepares you for it but doing it.
  • Quality and process improvement as a working method, not a slogan.
  • Staffing arithmetic — ratios, agency cost, overtime, turnover, and what each does to both the budget and the care.
  • Writing that survives a regulator, because a policy you wrote will be read back to you.

Advice

⚠⚠ Pick the major on where you want to work, not in the abstract. Health administration is the safe answer and the statute rewards it on the long-term care side. Business is the stronger answer for health plans, finance and revenue cycle. A clinical degree is the stronger answer for hospital operations, because you will be managing clinicians.

⚠⚠⚠ Plan for the master's from the start. Nearly half the degree-holders in this occupation have one, so treat the bachelor's as the first half rather than the destination — and if the executive track is the goal, get the CAHME-accredited one.

⚠ Do the bachelor's at a state college if one near you carries it. Twenty do. The money you do not spend on it is the money that pays for the master's that actually moves you.

And get operational experience early, in any setting. Scheduling, registration, billing, supply, a clinic front desk — this is a field where people who have never run anything are visible immediately, and a management degree without operating experience is a weak application.

⚠ If long-term care interests you, read s. 468.1695 before choosing a major. It is the one place on this path where the choice has a number attached.

programs.note: The named route — 24 Florida public institutions, 1,293 credentials a year, 741 bachelor's and 343 master's. ⚠⚠ And unusually available: 20 state colleges carry the upper-division coursework against 9 universities, so the degree can usually be finished near home at state-college tuition.

⚠⚠ The second-largest feeder in the Census data — 75,396 medical and health services managers hold a business undergraduate degree. ⚠ Genuinely the stronger choice for health plans, finance and revenue cycle; weaker on the nursing home side, where s. 468.1695 doubles the required training programme for a non-health major.

⚠⚠⚠ The largest real feeder and the least advertised. HEALTH is the biggest undergraduate field in this occupation at 169,319 people, and much of that is clinicians who crossed over. ⚠ A nurse moving into management arrives knowing what the operation does and is credible with the staff — which is the part a degree cannot supply.

⚠ The adjacent degree, constantly confused with this one. HIM owns the RECORD and carries real credentials (RHIT, RHIA); administration runs the ORGANISATION and carries none outside nursing homes. ⚠⚠ HIM is more credentialed and smaller; administration pays more and is far larger.

⚠ Where a great many people on this path actually start. Front-office staff who understand scheduling, insurance verification and referrals are exactly who gets promoted into practice management — and this is the degree that formalises it.

⚠ Not a route, but the same crossing happens here: EMS and fire agencies promote from the field into operations and administration. Named because the pattern generalises across every clinical service on this site — paramedics, respiratory therapists, radiographers and laboratory staff all arrive at this degree the same way.

courses.reason: Health Care Systems — 12 institutions, the most widely carried upper-division course in the prefix. How the American system is financed, organised and regulated; everything else assumes it.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers this subject at least three ways — HSA3111 (12 carriers), HSA3110 Health Administration (9) and HSA3113 US Health Care Systems (9). Register by number, and expect a transfer evaluator to need the syllabus.

courses.reason: Continuous Quality Improvement and Risk Management — 12 institutions, tied for the widest. Quality is not a slogan in this field; it is a regulated function with named methods and reportable measures.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as HSA4502 Health Care Risk Management at 9 institutions, which splits the same ground differently.

courses.reason: ⚠ Health Care Finance — 10 institutions. One of O*NET's four core tasks is fiscal operations, and this is the course that teaches it. Take it seriously even if finance is not why you came.
Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management — 10 institutions. Where claims, coding, denials and cash actually meet; the single most practically employable subject on this list.
Health Administration — 9 institutions. The alternative statewide framing of the systems course; several programmes use this instead of HSA3111.
Health Care Risk Management — 9 institutions. Incident reporting, liability, patient safety and the regulator's view of an adverse event.

Information Systems Management in Health Care — 8 institutions. The electronic health record is the operational system of the whole organisation, and managing it badly is how organisations fail quietly.

⚠ Health Administration Internship — 8 institutions. Operating experience is what distinguishes a hireable graduate here, and on the long-term care route a college-affiliated internship is one of the two ways s. 468.1695 lets you qualify.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ If nursing home administration is a possibility, ask whether this internship is structured to count toward the s. 468.1695 requirement — that is worth up to 1,000 hours.

courses.reason: Human Resource Management in Healthcare — 7 institutions. Staffing ratios, credentialing, agency cost and turnover: the largest line in almost every health care budget.
Leadership and Management in Healthcare — 7 institutions. Specifically about managing licensed professionals, which is the part that makes this different from general management.
Capstone: Health Administration — 7 institutions. The integrative project, and usually the strongest thing on a new graduate's application.
Health Care Informatics — 6 institutions. Data, reporting and analytics on the management side, and increasingly what separates candidates.
Healthcare Delivery Systems — 8 institutions, and lower division, so it is the way into the subject for a student still at the A.A. stage.
Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. ⚠ Not optional in practice: fiscal operations is a core task of the job and you cannot manage a budget you cannot read.
Principles of Microeconomics — 39 institutions. Health economics is the argument underneath every payer contract and every policy fight; this is where it starts.
Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Quality measurement, staffing analysis and outcomes reporting are statistical work, and the degree assumes it.
Principles of Management — 17 institutions. The general management foundation, and the course that overlaps most with the business-major route into this occupation.
Medical Terminology — 16 institutions. ⚠ Particularly if you are coming from the business or psychology side rather than a clinical one: you will be in rooms where nobody explains the vocabulary.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers this twice: HSC1531 at 16 institutions and HSC2531 at 8.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. A policy you wrote will be read back to you by a regulator; writing that survives that is a working skill here.

sources.note: ⚠⚠ The entrant-major data for this CHOICE path. Most common undergraduate fields: HEALTH 169,319, BUSINESS 75,396, PSYCHOLOGY 47,154. Attainment: bachelor's 263,934, ⚠ GRADUATE DEGREE 250,881, some college 112,767. ⚠ Data USA is a tabulation of ACS public-use microdata, not a primary publication; the counts are the survey's and the presentation is theirs. ⚠⚠ ACS records the field of degree for bachelor's degrees only.

sources.label: Section 468.1695, Florida Statutes — nursing home administrator licensure
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The statute that prices the major. A baccalaureate majoring in health care administration, health services administration or an equivalent major qualifies with a college-affiliated internship or a 1,000-hour training programme; any other bachelor's needs a 2,000-hour programme, or one year of qualifying management experience in a skilled nursing, hospital, hospice or 60-bed-plus assisted living facility plus 1,000 hours. ⚠ Examination at least twice a year, fee capped at $250.

sources.label: Section 468.1655, Florida Statutes — definitions
sources.note: ⚠⚠ The reason the licence matters: Florida defines a nursing home administrator as a person who is LICENSED to engage in the practice of nursing home administration in this state. ⚠ Hospital, clinic, group-practice, surgery-centre and health-plan management carry no equivalent Florida licence — so within one occupation, one setting is regulated and the rest are not.

sources.label: IPEDS Completions 2023 (C2023_A) — CIP 51.0701
sources.note: Health/Health Care Administration: 24 Florida public institutions, 1,293 credentials — 741 bachelor's, 343 master's, 135 associate, 72 short certificates. Largest producers UCF 276, FIU 274, FAU 180, UNF 133, then a long state-college tail: Miami Dade 55, Seminole State 45, Indian River 37, St Petersburg 36.

sources.label: SCNS statewide course file — the HSA prefix by sector
sources.note: ⚠⚠ Measured over the whole file: upper-division HSA coursework is carried by 20 Florida College System institutions against 9 State University System institutions. ⚠ For most baccalaureate subjects the ratio runs the other way, which is what makes this degree unusually reachable without transferring. ⚠ The systems course is numbered at least three ways — HSA3111 (12 carriers), HSA3110 (9), HSA3113 (9) — so register by number.

sources.label: CAHME — Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education
sources.note: ⚠ The accreditor the executive side of the field recognises for master's programmes. Florida's CAHME-accredited programmes are reported at UCF, FIU, UNF, UF and USF, all State University System. ⚠⚠ Verify the current list with CAHME rather than with a school — CAHME maintains the directory and the list changes. ⚠ There is no equivalent accreditation requirement for the bachelor's, and no Florida licence outside nursing home administration.
